title.en: Write the tests for a function

source.fr: Format « écris les tests » : très fréquent en entretien junior
source.en: "Write the tests" format: very common in junior interviews

mission.fr: Écrire des fonctions `test_...` qui couvrent la spécification, bornes comprises.
mission.en: Write `test_...` functions that cover the specification, boundaries included.

fr: Tes tests passent sur la vraie fonction.
Chacune des trois versions cassées est attrapée par au moins un test.
en: Your tests pass on the real function.
Each of the three broken versions is caught by at least one test.

prompt.fr: Écris tes tests ci-dessous. `days_since` et `NOW` sont fournis : n'écris pas la fonction. Utilise des `assert`.
prompt.en: Write your tests below. `days_since` and `NOW` are provided: do not write the function. Use `assert`.

questions.starter:
# Provided, do not rewrite it: your tests will be run against it and against broken versions.
# days_since(date_str, now) returns the whole days between date_str ("YYYY-MM-DD", UTC)
# and now, or None if date_str is unreadable or in the future.
from datetime import datetime, timezone

NOW = datetime(2026, 10, 22, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def test_today():
    assert days_since("2026-10-22", NOW) == 0

test_pass_on_real.fr: Tous tes tests passent sur la vraie fonction
test_pass_on_real.en: All your tests pass on the real function

test_catch_no_future_check.fr: Attrape la version qui accepte les dates futures
test_catch_no_future_check.en: Catches the version that accepts future dates

test_catch_off_by_one.fr: Attrape la version décalée d'un jour à partir de 30
test_catch_off_by_one.en: Catches the version off by one from 30 days

test_catch_crash_on_none.fr: Attrape la version qui plante sur `None`
test_catch_crash_on_none.en: Catches the version that crashes on `None`

fr: Teste les bornes : 30 jours pile, c'est là que se cachent les décalages.
Une date future, c'est un test à part entière.
en: Test the boundaries: exactly 30 days is where off-by-ones hide.
A future date deserves its own test.

explanation.fr:
Le point qui fait la différence : **rendre l'horloge injectable**, sinon le test dépend du jour où il tourne.

```python
NOW = datetime(2026, 10, 22, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

@pytest.mark.parametrize("date_str, expected", [
    ("2026-10-22", 0),
    ("2026-09-22", 30),     # la limite de retour, pile
    ("2026-09-21", 31),
    ("2026-10-25", -3),     # date future : documente le comportement actuel
    ("2026-02-30", None),
    ("", None),
    (None, None),
    ("22/10/2026", None),
])
def test_days_since(date_str, expected):
    assert _days_since(date_str, now=NOW) == expected
```

Ce qu'un CTO regarde : les bornes (29, 30, 31) et le test qui documente un comportement douteux au lieu de le cacher.
explanation.en:
The point that makes the difference: **make the clock injectable**, otherwise the test depends on the day it runs.

```python
NOW = datetime(2026, 10, 22, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

@pytest.mark.parametrize("date_str, expected", [
    ("2026-10-22", 0),
    ("2026-09-22", 30),     # the return limit, exactly
    ("2026-09-21", 31),
    ("2026-10-25", -3),     # future date: documents today's behaviour
    ("2026-02-30", None),
    ("", None),
    (None, None),
    ("22/10/2026", None),
])
def test_days_since(date_str, expected):
    assert _days_since(date_str, now=NOW) == expected
```

What a CTO looks at: the boundaries (29, 30, 31) and a test that documents doubtful behaviour instead of hiding it.
